accepted_reference.reason: Human reviewer preferred v5 over v6; v5 is the current aesthetic checkpoint before further automation work.

candidate_style_reference.reason: Human reviewer considered v10 very successful after the content-fit component reflow pass, but it should not become a reusable golden style until it survives additional papers.
promotion_criteria: passes nonvisual audit with no high or medium findings on at least two non-Kimi papers
human review confirms the style still feels polished when figures, tables, and evidence density differ
new cross-paper failures are converted into badcases before promotion

validation_cases.finding_summary: 56 low findings; no high or medium findings after wide-figure aspect-aware reflow, inline-table payload indexing, shallow-card internal spacing, and agenda read-path header clearance repairs.

core_principles.rule: Do not reparse a paper when summary, plan, slide_spec, figures, tables, and metrics are already available and reliable.
core_principles.why: The Kimi K2 parsing chain was already strong; from-scratch means a new slide story and visual system, not a new PDF understanding pass.

core_principles.rule: Build a content-complete inventory and rough slide story before optimizing aesthetics.
core_principles.why: A good-looking deck that drops tables, metrics, or proof objects fails the paper-reading task.

core_principles.rule: Choose the presentation archetype, deck structure, layout families, proof-object grammar, and component composition before tuning font sizes or local text density.
core_principles.why: The successful v5 iteration came from first establishing an academic paper-reading style system; v6 showed that local component resizing can hurt the whole-slide composition.

core_principles.rule: Keep typography roles deck-consistent, then fit real text into each component; if a local component becomes clearly too empty or too full, resize that component and reflow its same-slide siblings.
core_principles.why: v9 showed that single-page text tweaks are not enough: component size, internal spacing, and local page composition form one loop after content is inserted.

core_principles.rule: Every subjective complaint should be translated into a badcase, trigger signal, repair strategy, and regression check.
core_principles.why: The goal is not one manually corrected PPT, but a benchmark that helps future decks self-diagnose and improve.

core_principles.rule: For the current phase, use PPTX geometry, text, font, table, and layout metadata only; do not render pages or call a vision model.
core_principles.why: The user prefers preserving good component composition and avoiding costly screenshot/vision loops; metadata checks can catch many text, overlap, and density risks.

core_principles.rule: If an automatic heuristic produces a version the human reviewer dislikes, preserve the preferred version and record the heuristic as risky.
core_principles.why: v6 tried to optimize read path and sparse evidence cards, but the user found v5 better overall.

core_principles.rule: A style that succeeds on one paper becomes a candidate reference, not a golden baseline, until it passes other papers with different evidence shapes.
core_principles.why: A visual system can fit one paper's content distribution while failing on denser figures, different tables, or less regular proof objects.

human_findings: No academic title slide.
No agenda / roadmap slide.
Most pages repeated a large right-side proof panel.
Short text evidence appeared inside oversized empty panels.
Tables were sometimes summarized instead of rendered as complete table evidence.
The system lacked a deck-render review loop.
repairs: Add title, agenda, section, and closing slides.
Introduce layout families beyond a single right proof panel.
Treat figures, tables, text evidence, and metrics as distinct proof objects.
Add visual audit manifest and render-review hook.

human_findings: Black-and-white palette felt dull and lifeless.
Cover black bar and meaningless metric chips looked unattractive.
Agenda number buttons were too heavy.
Some limitation / motivation / method evidence panels remained sparse.
Some table and card components overlapped body text.
Metric layouts were inconsistent across pages.
repairs: Switch to warm academic palette with teal, soft gold, clay, and paper tones.
Replace heavy black cover treatment with a lighter cover system.
Replace agenda dots with module markers and a deck map.
Route short proof text to compact evidence cards.
Add table-bottom review targets and overlap-oriented badcase rules.

human_findings: The deck became much better aesthetically.
Cover right rail should show paper highlights, not only source inventory counts.
Evidence-note triplets repeated too often and needed more variation.
A table panel still overlapped support text on one page.
Some body text felt too small or sparse.
repairs: Derive cover-ready paper highlights from existing checkpoints.
Vary evidence card layouts: right stack, bottom notes, mosaic, and compact cards.
Move table panels below claim/support text with clear gutters.
Add text snapshot fallback for review when PNG rendering is unavailable.

human_findings: Cover paper highlights were good, but source-depth chips at the bottom were unnecessary.
Agenda read path should use visual flow components instead of dry text.
A three-card evidence mosaic needed better proportions.
Left-side evidence triplets felt less formal than right or bottom placement.
PowerPoint rendering still had local COM reliability issues.
repairs: Remove cover source-depth chips and keep paper highlights prominent.
Use compact read-path nodes instead of a plain text arrow chain.
Prefer right-side and bottom evidence placements; avoid left evidence triplets for formal academic pages.
Keep renderer failures explicit and continue exporting text snapshots.

human_findings: This version was considered the most pleasing checkpoint.
The deck should be saved before further experiments.
repairs: Treat rough_draft_v5 as the current accepted benchmark reference.
Use v5 as the regression target for future aesthetic changes.

human_findings: v6 was less attractive than v5 and felt strange.
The 2x2 read path and aggressive sparse-card resizing did not improve the overall deck.
repairs: Rollback v6 visual heuristics.
Record that local density optimization can hurt composition and should require human or visual-regression approval.

human_findings: Cover highlight bodies sat too far below their labels, weakening the colored-rail pairing.
The agenda read path correctly wrapped to two rows, but the columns were too far apart and labels were not visually anchored under nodes.
Bottom evidence cards could become too tall after text fitting; this should be treated as local component reflow, not deck-wide font drift.
Figure component labels sat too close to rounded panel boundaries.
repairs: Add paired label-body spacing checks for cover highlight rail stacks.
Add 2x2 read-path grid checks for column gap, row gap, and label-center drift.
Add content-fit component frame checks so sparse cards can shrink locally and trigger same-slide reflow.
Add component label boundary-inset checks for figure/table proof panels.

human_findings: Human reviewer considered the v10 PPT very successful and aesthetically satisfying on the Kimi K2 primary case.
The current style should be preserved as a candidate reference but not promoted to golden baseline before cross-paper validation.
repairs: Record v10 as a candidate style reference with promotion criteria instead of replacing the accepted v5 checkpoint immediately.
Use the mHC paper as the next validation case for detecting cross-paper style failures.
Keep the human-in-the-loop loop active: generate, inspect, translate complaints into badcases, then repair and rerun.

human_findings: Directly applying the v10 visual style to mHC initially produced many text overflow findings because mHC claims, author list, highlights, and conclusion evidence are longer and more theoretical.
The style grammar itself did not trigger geometry or optical-balance failures after repair; the main cross-paper issue was text compression and narrow-card fitting.
repairs: Add cross-paper claim/support word limits by proof type.
Compact long author lists on cover slides.
Remove Kimi-specific closing copy and derive closing takeaway from paper highlights.
Route non-metric closing summaries to evidence cards instead of metric grids.
Use compact typography for narrow evidence-card stacks.

human_findings: Wide figures such as Figure 4 and Figure 6 were forced into the generic right-side rounded rectangle, making long horizontal diagrams visually unclear and sometimes distorted.
A slide_spec inline table with real rows was referenced by its display title, but the renderer only indexed extracted asset-table ids, so the proof panel fell back to a near-empty text block.
repairs: Route figure proof objects by source image aspect ratio: very wide figures use a long bottom proof panel rather than a side proof panel.
Fit figure images into their content box while preserving the original aspect ratio.
Index curated inline table rows alongside extracted asset tables so title-referenced tables still render as native PPT tables.
Add benchmark badcases for wide-figure layout mismatch and inline table payload indexing failures.

human_findings: On the conclusion slide, the right-side evidence note cards were shallower than earlier evidence cards, but they reused the same fixed label/body offsets.
The labels looked acceptable, yet the body text sat too low inside each rounded card because internal spacing did not adapt to the local card height.
repairs: Add a compact-shallow evidence card mode that reduces label/body gap and gives the body text a taller box inside shallow cards.
Add a nonvisual audit rule for shallow evidence cards whose internal label/body spacing or bottom padding does not scale to the frame.
Record the lesson that component internals must be proportional to local component size, not only globally consistent by component type.

human_findings: The mHC v12 deck was considered essentially finished, but the agenda Read path header felt slightly too close to the P/M/E/T flow nodes.
This is a low-risk polish issue: it does not break structure, but it weakens the small rail's hierarchy and breathing room.
repairs: Lift the agenda Read path header while preserving the existing two-row flow node grid.
Add a metadata-only audit rule for Read path header-to-node clearance so this kind of final polish can be tracked without screenshot review.
Record that not every human discomfort needs a major repair; some become scoped micro-polish rules.

trigger_signals: deck has no title role slide
first slide lacks paper title
badcase_rules.root_cause: Paper-reading deck was treated as content pages only.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Always generate a polished academic title slide.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Slide 1 has role=title and includes paper title, author/team, and a concise deck thesis.

trigger_signals: no agenda / roadmap slide
sections are not visible before content slides
badcase_rules.root_cause: Narrative planning was not reflected in the PPT.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Generate a roadmap page from section buckets and slide counts.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Slide 2 has role=agenda and lists Motivation, Method, Experiments, and Takeaways or equivalent paper-specific modules.

trigger_signals: dominant layout family ratio > 0.45
max consecutive same layout >= 4
large proof panel appears in the same position on most slides
badcase_rules.root_cause: Renderer reused one macro layout for unrelated evidence types.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Rotate layout families by role and proof type: right proof, bottom proof, table bottom, metric cards, evidence stack, evidence mosaic.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Visual audit reports varied layout families and no long run of identical content layouts.

trigger_signals: proof_object.type == text_evidence
proof text is short
assigned proof panel area is large
badcase_rules.root_cause: Short text evidence was treated like a figure/table proof object.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use compact evidence notes, bottom cards, or mosaic cards instead of a large empty proof panel.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Short evidence pages do not show mostly empty oversized rounded rectangles.

trigger_signals: table proof object exists
native table has no parsed rows
slide only contains a textual table summary
badcase_rules.root_cause: Table extraction was not carried through to the renderer.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Preserve parsed table rows in content inventory and render them as native PPT tables.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Table proof slides show row/column grammar and include at least one non-header row when source rows exist.

trigger_signals: table or proof panel intersects body text box
shape bounding boxes overlap above threshold
render review shows text covered by card/panel
badcase_rules.root_cause: Proof object y-position or height did not reserve enough gutter for claim/support text.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Move proof panels lower, reduce proof height, or split content across alternate layouts.
badcase_rules.regression_check: No high-risk overlap among title, claim, support, table, and proof panel bounding boxes.

trigger_signals: palette uses mostly black, white, and gray
section dividers use full dark backgrounds repeatedly
accent colors are absent or semantically unused
badcase_rules.root_cause: Academic restraint was interpreted as monochrome.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use a restrained warm academic palette with semantic accents.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Deck uses warm paper background plus 2-3 muted accent colors without becoming over-decorated.

trigger_signals: cover highlights only counts figures/tables/metrics
cover side rail lacks paper-specific contribution summary
badcase_rules.root_cause: Cover used source inventory rather than paper value proposition.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Derive 3 paper highlights from parsed checkpoints: core result, scale, design edge, or evidence scope.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Cover side rail includes paper-specific highlights, not just source-depth counters.

trigger_signals: agenda right panel contains only plain arrow text
read path has no visual rhythm
badcase_rules.root_cause: Narrative flow was rendered as dry copy instead of a component.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use compact flow nodes/icons while preserving balance; do not overcomplicate if the panel becomes awkward.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Agenda side panel shows readable flow components and does not feel crowded.

trigger_signals: new heuristic shrinks or rearranges cards but human preference worsens
visual composition feels less stable than accepted reference
badcase_rules.root_cause: A local non-visual metric optimized sparse text boxes but ignored whole-slide composition.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Gate density-based visual changes behind accepted-reference comparison and selective rendered review.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Changes that alter accepted v5 visual grammar require either improved visual score or explicit human approval.

trigger_signals: support/body role font size is below metadata floor
support/body role font size falls below preferred band while capacity is safe
badcase_rules.root_cause: A readable academic composition was kept, but secondary prose was authored with too little typographic presence.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Increase body/support font size, improve hierarchy, or shorten copy before changing the component box.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Body/support text clears the metadata floor and no new near-overflow finding is introduced.

trigger_signals: evidence card body font size is below metadata floor
cover highlight or evidence note body sits below preferred font band
badcase_rules.root_cause: Compact evidence cards preserved the v5 composition but made card copy feel underpowered.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Raise card label/body typography within the existing card group and split notes only if capacity becomes risky.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Evidence card text clears the card font floor while card group geometry remains close to the accepted reference.

trigger_signals: claim/support/card text roles are too close in font size
component labels visually compete with evidence body text
badcase_rules.root_cause: The slide has the right components but insufficient type contrast between claim, support, labels, and notes.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Adjust font hierarchy and weight first; avoid moving components unless overlap or capacity fails.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Claim remains dominant, support is readable, and card body text has clearer hierarchy.

trigger_signals: low_text_density finding on evidence card text
card copy has very few words while the card group has accepted geometry
badcase_rules.root_cause: A card sized for a reading note received a thin label or fragment instead of useful evidence copy.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Enrich the card body from existing support/proof text or rebalance reading notes; do not shrink the whole card group.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Card information density improves without changing the accepted component composition.

trigger_signals: evidence cards have strongly uneven word counts
one note is near capacity while a sibling card is sparse
badcase_rules.root_cause: Support text was split mechanically instead of being allocated to balanced reading notes.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Redistribute note copy, shorten the dense card, and enrich sparse siblings before resizing cards.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Sibling card word counts move into a comparable range and no overflow finding appears.

trigger_signals: a repair changes component size or position when only low-density findings were present
no overlap, out-of-bounds, unreadable table, or repeated-layout structural finding exists
badcase_rules.root_cause: The repair loop treated low density as a geometry problem and risked repeating the v6 regression.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Reject geometry changes unless a structural finding exists; prefer typography, line breaks, copy allocation, or notes splitting.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Low-density-only repairs preserve component geometry and update only typography/copy fields.

trigger_signals: cover title/support metadata remains below the cover comfort font band
right highlight rail typography is lifted but left title narrative is not lifted as a group
badcase_rules.root_cause: Cover typography was tuned per component, so the right rail could improve while the left title, author, thesis, and focus copy stayed visually underpowered.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Lift the cover's left-side typography as one hierarchy group, then recheck wrapping and vertical spacing before moving components.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Cover left title narrative clears the comfort band and no new wrap, overlap, or out-of-bounds warning appears.

trigger_signals: agenda read-path labels sit in one row with too little horizontal gap
four compact flow buttons are squeezed into a narrow side panel
badcase_rules.root_cause: The flow component only knew one horizontal layout and did not choose a two-row arrangement when labels became crowded.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Switch compact flow nodes to a 2x2 or two-row path when label gaps fall below the comfort threshold; do not solve this by shrinking labels.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Read-path node labels have comfortable gaps or use two rows while preserving the P/M/E/T sequence.

trigger_signals: a rounded container has strongly uneven top and bottom padding around its internal content stack
metric or evidence cards occupy only the upper or lower part of their parent panel
badcase_rules.root_cause: The audit treated each textbox separately and did not evaluate the visual center of the grouped text/card stack inside a container.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Rebalance the internal stack or enrich sparse cards before changing the whole slide macro-layout; allow slight optical bias for emphasized values.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Container text/card stacks stay within the optical padding tolerance without forcing mathematically perfect centering.

trigger_signals: metric value and label are positioned with a card-height proportional gap
two text lines inside one metric card feel disconnected after the card gets taller
badcase_rules.root_cause: Metric card internals used fixed y ratios rather than a value+label text stack with a stable gap.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Lay out metric value and label as one optical text stack with a fixed gap; keep the value slightly dominant rather than blindly centering both lines.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Metric cards preserve value dominance while the value-label gap remains within the stack comfort threshold.

trigger_signals: many slides have below-ideal typography findings even though no individual slide has a severe font violation
support, card body, or cover metadata repeatedly feels slightly too small across the deck
badcase_rules.root_cause: Low-severity typography warnings were ranked locally, so a deck-wide weak type scale never became a repair target.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Run a deck-level typography pass that safely lifts repeated roles, checks capacity, then repairs line breaks or copy allocation if needed.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Deck-level below-ideal typography count decreases without introducing near-overflow, overlap, or geometry-only repairs.

trigger_signals: a label and its explanatory body belong to the same semantic rail but their starts are too far apart
colored marker, label, and explanation no longer read as one grouped item
badcase_rules.root_cause: Typography repair lifted or moved text boxes independently instead of treating label and explanation as one optical stack.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Move the body closer to the label within the same rail group before moving the whole group or changing font size.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Cover highlight label-body top delta stays within the paired-stack threshold while each group still aligns with its colored rail.

trigger_signals: 2x2 read-path nodes have an overly wide column gap
row gap is too tight after wrapping
node labels are not centered under their circles
badcase_rules.root_cause: The repair knew to wrap the flow into two rows but did not define grid proportions and label anchoring rules.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use a compact 2x2 flow grid with smaller column gap, larger row gap, and label boxes centered on node centers.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Read-path grid passes column-gap, row-gap, column-to-row ratio, and label-center tolerance checks.

trigger_signals: agenda slide contains a Read path header
Read path header bottom is too close to the first-row flow nodes
human reviewer describes the rail as slightly cramped even though node alignment is correct
badcase_rules.root_cause: The flow grid was repaired for node/label alignment, but the local header-to-flow breathing room was not part of the component contract.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Lift the Read path header slightly while preserving the existing flow node grid and right rail composition.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Agenda Read path header clears the nearest P/M/E/T node by the configured minimum gap.

trigger_signals: a card frame remains much taller than the fitted label/body stack
local evidence card feels empty after text has been inserted
badcase_rules.root_cause: The system froze component dimensions before seeing the real text, then tried to judge the result only by font size or text density.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Keep deck-wide typography roles stable, shrink or expand the affected local frame after content fitting, and reflow sibling components on the same slide.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Card frame extra height stays within the fitted-text threshold and sibling card alignment remains coherent.

trigger_signals: a shallow narrow evidence card reuses the same label/body offsets as taller or wider cards
body text bottom padding is too small inside a card
label appears acceptable but body text feels visually low or detached in the local frame
badcase_rules.root_cause: Component internals were governed by fixed offsets per card type rather than spacing rules that respond to the local card height.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use a height-aware compact card mode for shallow narrow cards: reduce label/body gap, increase body text box height, and preserve deck-wide typography roles.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Shallow narrow evidence cards pass label/body gap and bottom-padding checks without changing unrelated evidence card layouts.

trigger_signals: figure/table label sits too close to a rounded panel edge
component heading appears to cross or kiss the boundary curve
badcase_rules.root_cause: Proof-object labels were placed by a fixed small offset without accounting for rounded-corner optical padding.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Inset proof-object labels farther from rounded panel corners and reduce the content viewport if needed.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Figure/table component labels clear the minimum boundary inset before figure/table content is fitted.

trigger_signals: candidate style passes the primary paper but produces high text overflow findings on another paper
long author lists, theoretical claims, dense support paragraphs, or conclusion evidence exceed the fixed style frames
non-metric closing evidence is routed into metric card grammar
badcase_rules.root_cause: The visual style was reusable, but the text compression contract was tuned to the primary paper's content shape.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Set claim/support/highlight word limits by proof type, compact long author lists, derive closing copy from the current paper, and use compact typography for narrow evidence stacks.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Cross-paper validation decks have no high/medium text overflow findings while preserving the candidate style grammar.

trigger_signals: figure proof object has an image aspect ratio above the wide-figure threshold
layout family is still visual_left or visual_right
figure is inserted with both fixed width and fixed height that do not match the original aspect ratio
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer treated all figures as the same proof-object type and ignored the source image shape when choosing the component frame.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Compute figure aspect ratio from the extracted asset and route very wide figures to a long bottom proof panel; fit the image inside the box without distortion.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Very wide figure assets use figure_bottom_wide or another horizontal figure layout, and inserted picture dimensions preserve the source aspect ratio.

trigger_signals: PPTX picture shape aspect ratio differs materially from the embedded source image aspect ratio
figure was inserted with both fixed width and fixed height instead of a fitted aspect-preserving box
human reviewer describes the figure as squeezed, stretched, or unclear after resizing
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer filled the component viewport by forcing picture width and height rather than fitting the source image into the available box.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Compute a centered fit rectangle from source image dimensions and component content bounds; supply fitted width and height that preserve the source aspect ratio.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Nonvisual audit reports no figure_picture_aspect_distortion findings for generated figure proof panels.

trigger_signals: slide proof object references a table by display title rather than extracted asset id
slide_spec inline table contains rows but table_index lookup returns no rows
table proof panel renders as a fallback text block instead of a native table
badcase_rules.root_cause: The proof-object resolver could select curated slide tables, but the table renderer only indexed extracted asset tables.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Index curated inline table rows together with extracted table assets before rendering and auditing table proof objects.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Title-referenced inline tables render as native PPT tables with row/column grammar instead of empty-looking text panels.

good_signals: title, agenda, section, content, and closing slides feel intentional
deck looks like an academic presentation rather than generated notes
restrained but lively warm academic colors
proof objects can appear right, bottom, compact, table, metric, or mosaic depending on content
bad_signals: same right proof panel on most pages
left evidence triplets on formal pages if they reduce gravitas

good_signals: wide figures use frames that respect their original shape
metrics preserve value, label, and context
text evidence uses appropriately sized cards
bad_signals: wide figures are squeezed into side panels or distorted

good_signals: title, claim, support, card text, table text, and footer have clear hierarchy
sparse text does not create awkward empty containers
component frames adapt after content fitting without changing deck-wide type roles
bad_signals: card text too sparse for card size
label/body stacks or proof labels feel visually detached from their component

good_signals: visual audit manifest identifies high-risk pages
text snapshots or rendered screenshots are produced when possible
bad_signals: system cannot inspect generated deck artifacts

good_signals: from-scratch deck does not copy golden baseline skeleton
new visual system preserves parsed paper content

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Reuse parsed checkpoints to collect paper metadata, thesis, highlights, sections, figures, tables, metrics, and evidence links.
non_visual_checks: required checkpoint files exist
paper title and author/team are present
figures, tables, and metrics have stable identifiers
core sections cover motivation, method, experiments, and takeaway
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Return to inventory construction; do not redesign slides until missing evidence is recovered from existing checkpoints.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Decide that the output is an academic paper-reading deck with title, agenda, section dividers, content modules, and closing slide.
non_visual_checks: slide roles include title, agenda, section_opener, content roles, and closing
agenda modules map to contiguous slide ranges
section counts are plausible for the requested slide budget
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Regenerate section buckets and slide-role map before touching visual components.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Assign one main claim, concise support text, and one matching proof object to each content slide.
non_visual_checks: each content slide has exactly one dominant claim
support text is not empty and is not a duplicate of the claim
proof object type matches the slide role
table, figure, and metric slides retain source references
title-referenced inline tables with rows remain renderable proof payloads
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Repair slide spec content first; do not hide semantic gaps with layout decoration.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Define palette, typography hierarchy, layout families, evidence card grammar, metric grammar, table grammar, and forbidden baseline-like skeletons.
non_visual_checks: layout family distribution is varied but not random
accepted component proportions are preserved unless a structural rule fails
colors and component roles follow the style contract
new deck does not collapse into the golden baseline macro skeleton
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Change style tokens or layout assignment rules; avoid ad-hoc per-slide resizing as the first fix.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Insert real slide text into the chosen components, then adjust only components whose fitted text makes them visibly too empty, too full, detached, or boundary-unsafe.
non_visual_checks: paired label/body stacks use stable local gaps
2x2 flow grids keep compact columns, breathable rows, and centered labels
agenda read-path header keeps enough clearance above the flow nodes
component frames are not substantially overallocated after fitted text height is estimated
shallow evidence cards scale internal label/body spacing to local card height
figure/table labels clear rounded component boundaries
very wide figures are assigned a horizontal proof frame instead of a side frame
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Resize or reposition the local component and its same-slide siblings; preserve deck-wide type roles and avoid changing unrelated pages.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Inspect generated PPTX as a layout program: shape geometry, font sizes, text capacity, table grammar, metric grammar, and overlap risk.
non_visual_checks: no high-risk text/proof/table overlap
font-size floors pass by role
near-capacity and low-density findings are classified separately
tables preserve rows and columns
inline table rows from slide_spec are indexed when no extracted table id matches
wide figure images preserve source aspect ratio when fitted into PPTX picture boxes
metrics preserve value, label, and context
paired text stacks, shallow-card internal spacing, component frame fit, and component boundary inset pass local optical checks
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Emit badcase hits and rank only the top issues for the next repair pass.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Repair the highest-impact problems without breaking the accepted overall composition.
non_visual_checks: repair changes are limited to top 1-3 badcases
copy and font fixes are preferred before resizing accepted components
component geometry changes require a structural or content-fit failure such as overlap, unreadable table, missing content, failed flow grid, boundary violation, or overallocated frame
same-slide sibling components are reflowed after any local frame resize
new output is compared against accepted-reference rules
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Stop when high/medium findings are gone or when another repair would alter the style contract without evidence.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Before promoting a successful style to a golden baseline, rerun it on papers with different figure, table, metric, and text-evidence profiles.
non_visual_checks: candidate style passes nonvisual audit without high or medium findings on each validation paper
new findings are separated into style-specific failures versus paper-content extraction failures
human reviewer approves the contact-sheet rhythm on at least two non-primary papers
every recurring cross-paper complaint becomes a badcase before promotion
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Keep the style as a candidate reference, add or tune badcases, and rerun validation instead of declaring a golden baseline from one paper.

non_visual_self_repair_policy.design_assumption: Treat PPTX as a structured layout program. The system cannot literally see the slide, but it can inspect the objects, positions, sizes, fonts, text length, tables, and role metadata that produce the slide.
detectable_without_screenshots: missing title, agenda, section, or closing roles
agenda modules not aligned with slide ranges
claim/support/proof object missing or mismatched

repair_priority_ladder: Fix content correctness first: missing evidence, unsupported claims, table rows, metric values.
Fix structural deck grammar second: title, agenda, section ranges, slide role balance.
Fix semantic matching third: claim/support/proof object alignment.
Fix typography fourth: font floors, deck-level comfort band, text splitting, line breaks, copy allocation.
Fix content-fit optical balance fifth: paired label/body proximity, value-label gap, card padding, and proof-label boundary inset.
Fix local component frame sizing sixth when fitted text makes a card clearly too empty or too full; then reflow same-slide siblings.
Fix geometry only when necessary: overlap, out-of-bounds, unreadable table, failed flow grid, boundary inset violation, or repeated layout family.
Change accepted component proportions only when the audit shows a structural or content-fit failure, not merely low text density.
Change the visual system only through a new style-contract revision and compare against the accepted reference.
stop_conditions: no high or medium non-visual findings remain
remaining findings are low-density or low-font risks that would require style-contract changes
a repair would improve local density but violate accepted-reference composition
content_score, visual_layout_score, and nonvisual audit are stable across two attempts
